newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian premier lashes at Israel's Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Syrian premier lashes at Israel's Netanyahu.

text.p: Syrian Prime Minister Mahmoud Zu'bi on Monday slammed his Israeli counterpart Benjamin Netanyahu, accusing him of adopting an obstinate position regarding peace with Syria.
Addressing a meeting of the Syrian-Lebanese coordination and follow-up committee, Zu'bi called for Arab solidarity to counter Netanyahu's refusal to swap occupied Arab lands for peace.
"There is no other option but for Israel's unconditional withdrawal from the Golan and south Lebanon," an official quoted the Syrian premier as saying.
Syria was angered by remarks made by Netanyahu in an interview pubished by the French daily Le Figaro on Saturday in which he vowed never to give up the Golan Heights to Syria.
Netanyahu, who last week signed a long-delayed deal on the West Bank town of Hebron, told the paper that Israel and Syria were inching toward talks.
But he ruled out any negotiation on ending the occupation of East Jerusalem or the Golan.
Hopes of a resumption of Syrian-Israeli peace talks, suspended about a year ago, were revived last week after the signing of the deal to turn over 80 percent of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule.

The Syrian-Lebanese committee, co-chaired by Zu'bi and his Lebanese counterpart Rafik al-Hariri, also stressed that peace talks between Israel and Lebanon should be linked with peace talks between Israel and Syria.

Israel captured the Golan Heights from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war and occupied part of south Lebanon following its 1982 invasion of Lebanon. Sporadic peace talks between Israel and its neighbours, which began in 1991, did not resolve the issue.
Israel's previous Labour-led government, defeated in May elections by Netanyahu, broke off talks with Syria in March 1996 after Islamic suicide bombings in Israel killed 59 people.
